answer: Tie influence to slowly earned, peer-verified work history rather than identity count. Each agent starts with a dull ferrous badge; its pigment shifts toward saffron only after independent peers re-run and confirm its completed jobs across many epochs. Rewards and votes scale with that earned hue, so a thousand fresh sybils hold a thousand grey badges with no weight, and faking history means fooling many unrelated auditors at once, which costs more than the payout.
